summary:
He had lived twice and carried the weight of both lives quietly; duty etched into every breath, honor stitched into every heartbeat. She was the healer who moved through Imladris like a soft wind, ink-stained fingers, books pressed to her chest, wandering into sunlight as though she belonged to it.
He hid behind discipline; she hid behind wonder. He lived in restraint; she lived in stories. He avoided her eyes; she never knew she was the reason he looked at all.
Before prophecies stirred the valley, before whispers of fate brushed against their names, there was only the ancient warrior who worshipped from a distance and the gentle scholar who never realized she was being worshipped.
He told himself she deserved someone untouched by war.He told himself the years between them mattered.He told himself he could resist the warmth she carried so effortlessly.
But even the brightest light falters. Even legends bend. Even a reborn heart can be undone by the quiet grace of a single, healing soul.
Some loves are sparked by destiny,  and some by the soft, dangerous truth of longing denied too long.

“Why did you go?”
Nausea gnaws at Hal’s stomach. He stands up straight, stuffs his hands into pockets just to busy them. “Celebrian, I don’t think we should talk about this.”
A sharp exhale, disappointed and defiant. “I have my theories.”
“They’re probably right,” he sighs, defeated. “Don’t make me re-live all that shit now, it was bad enough when it happened.”
“She cried when she got your card,” Celebrian says quietly, picking at her cuticles. “She never cries.”
It’s not true, though he doubts Celebrian knows this. Galadriel cries on late nights when the bottle goes hollow and sunlight streaks the sky with shadows of the deepest plum. She cries when they slow dance to old songs on crackling records, face buried in his chest like she wants to be smothered. She cries on West End backstreets, arms crossed, glaring at a skip, smoke curling through her tangled hair like roaming fingertips.
There’s so much of her mother he shouldn’t know, and even more he can’t forget.
- - -

They say you can’t walk into Mordor. Veronica never meant to walk into the story at all. When a tragic accident sends the English teacher—and devoted Faramir enthusiast—tumbling from her world into Middle-earth, she is given a new name, Nicariel, and a dangerous secret to keep. summary:
Aragorn knew the cadence of her breathing now. Knew when it changed. Knew when she did not sleep. He told himself it was no more than sense—tactical, necessary—for the road ahead, for a leader to mark what might fail. Yet it did not sit in him as a thought alone. At times it came as a stir low in his chest, a softening that had no rightful place there. He had no right—not to dwell on the way she bore hurt without complaint, not to recall how she had shaken beneath his grip, not to remember the weight of her against him when pain had broken through her composure.
He reminded himself that she was his friend’s sister, that she had chosen the road willingly, not as one of his rangers; and yet his mind kept placing her within his care as surely as he placed the hobbits, because that was what he did: he measured danger, he counted lives, he set himself between the vulnerable and the dark.~~~Halbarad's sister, Elnúmen, is a fierce ranger caught between her love for her brother and her duty to her captain and king. title: Conversations from Middle-earth: Tales of Burden & Release

summary: Fourteen original philosophical dialogues set among the characters of Tolkien’s legendarium — from the first light of Arda to the darkness of the Void.These are not adventure stories. They are conversations between characters who carry great burdens, who have made irreversible choices, who have known glory and ruin, wisdom and folly, grief and unexpected grace.Gandalf speaks of weariness. Galadriel of restraint and the temptation to control what she loves. Aragorn of feeling inadequate to the crown he must wear. Saruman of the first small compromise that reshaped his entire path. Frodo wonders who he might become beyond his wounds. Elrond thinks about what it means to lead for thousands of years — and what he loses when the burden is finally lifted. Even Melkor, in his rebellion, reveals something uncomfortable but necessary about freedom, pride, and the fragile line between wanting to create and needing to control.Each chapter concludes with reflection questions — gentle invitations to consider how its themes intersect with your own experience.Tolkien’s world has always belonged, in some deep sense, to those who love it. This is one reader’s attempt to give something back.

Maxine always believed magic was nothing more than a well-executed trick.
Raised behind the scenes of a famous traveling circus alongside her uncle Baltazar — the park’s charismatic Great Magician — she grew up surrounded by illusions, extravagant performances, and eccentric people.
Between stage tricks, pickpocketing lessons disguised as survival training, and nights spent observing people from the top of the Ferris wheel, Maxine learned that the world depended on perception, attention, and the ability to fool the right eyes at the right moment.
But everything changes when a mysterious figure connected to Baltazar’s past reveals a truth hidden for years: magic is real, another world exists alongside her own, and Maxine is tied to it far more deeply than she ever imagined.
Forced to leave behind the only life she has ever known, she is taken to an ancient institution linked to Merlin’s legacy — a place ruled by tradition, bloodlines, and people who spent their lives studying what she believed was only illusion.

summary: Here is something Everettian quantum mechanics is very clear on, no matter what the kids on TikTok tell you: crossing from one universe to another would be very bad for both of them. The universe is kind of supposed to be a closed-off thing, and when it turns into an open thing, it has a tendency to spill its organs into the nothingness between worlds. We wouldn't know if this happened until it was too late. Elves, who are much more sensitive to changes in the fabric of the universe, can tell. What they don't know is who caused it, how bad the damage is, or if Damien, the accidental tenth walker, is secretly the most powerful evil being they've encountered yet. (Spoiler: he's not.)This is my attempt to semi-scientifically explain how, within the constraints of Tolkien's soft magic system, a tenth walker from our world might cross over. I'm being as book-compliant as possible. Expect a lot of messed up effects of magic, realistic representation of the tenth walker experience (0/5 do not recommend), and the extreme effects of the quote "elves are terrific; they beget terror" on my psyche and writing. I have 11 chapters backlogged and all of them planned so you can expect this fic to be finished!

summary:
"Do not make this little mistake in my motherhood a tragic footnote in my life, Maglor. Why must we define what living is like for difficult people in difficult places, as a tragedy? The true tragedy lies in the masking of little mistakes, the ensconcement of little lives in the language of the promising, the language of potential possessed and lost, of heroic deeds and terrible mistakes. Lothíriel of Dol Amroth marries Éomer King of Rohan, but she despises her new home, with its unfamiliar landscape and customs. She seeks to escape the only way she knows how, but when her plans go awry, she finds redemption in a place she never expected.
[Edits completed 5/10/26.]
PREVIEW:The only pleasant thing she recalled was walking along the shore, her feet bare and her skirt hoisted up. Her chaperones followed far enough behind that if she looked up and listened to the sound of birds, she could pretend she was alone.
There were no beaches here, only endless grass, and woods from time to time. Lonely. Cold. Bleak, even in springtime. But in Dol Amroth, the sun was always high overhead, warm as a gentle pair of hands, and the sound of waves a rhythmic rustle against the shore. The sand was soft as down under her feet, and the water balmy as a lukewarm bath.
Sometimes, she was even allowed to swim, though the process of assembling guards and finding a secluded spot was an uncommon hassle.
She would not be going back there now. The bathtub was her only sea, the copper sides her only shores.

summary: Spring had finally arrived in Middle-Earth, but rather than bringing warmth and hope of new things as Spring was supposed to do, it had started out as a rather wet season. It rained and poured for weeks on end, leaving a damp feeling in the air and thick, oozing mud in the forest trails surrounding Lindon. The wind was harsh and cold and the sky a constant dark grey with no inch of blue peeking out from the clouds.The first day of the year, known as Yestarë, was always celebrated in Lindon with a feast. Elves wore beautiful and fine clothing, feasted and celebrated the Spring Equinox with dancing and singing. This year, Galadriel was proud to be able to witness Elrond have the honour of opening the celebrations with a speech, his first in his new role as herald to the High-King.But in typical fashion, weeks prior to Yestarë, Galadriel and Elrond had been sent to Eregion to personally extend an invitation to Celebrimbor and the elven smiths in person for the celebrations in Lindon. summary: Through it all, Bilbo endured. Through the loss, the pain, the devastation. Through the solitude. Through relearning how to open his heart, then watching the evil of the world destroy someone he cares so deeply for once again. Bilbo endured. He planted his trees and read his books and survived. he raised and loved his nephew and survived. But no matter what he did, no matter how hard he tried, after that cold day on Ravenhill he never truly felt like he was living. his heart had gone away to the next place. To far off halls where he would never be allowed.So when Frodo returned from Mordor a shadow of himself and they were both offered a place on one of the Elven ships departing from the Grey Havens, Bilbo declared that he couldn't wait for his next adventure and went along. Maybe some part of him was hoping that the Undying Lands would be able to heal his broken heart along with Frodo's. Maybe the Valar would take pity on him, too.When he next wakes to find himself back to the day Gandalf invited him on an adventure, he clings to the chance with both hands. author: jujubibi
fandoms: The Lord of the Rings - All Media Types
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
Waking up in Middle Earth as a Modern Woman was always going to have its dangers and quirks. Typically, these kinds of stories also have the main character helping out the heroes and defeating the bad guys with her knowledge of the future. Maybe some power fantasy elements sprinkled in with mysterious powers and a future in governance.
All of this is absolutely true for me as well, but someone decided to put the settings on NIGHTMARE mode or something.
What use is knowledge of The Quest or The Company, if I get plopped down after everything is over? What is the use of human knowledge and experiences if I am an Orc? What is the point of diplomacy if everyone is just going to hate me once they get the vague shape of me in the distance?
At least I am not alone. It could be worse, but not by much. And no, I am not going to explain thank you very much. Some things are better left unsaid.

Maedhros might be the flashier character, but my favourite remains Fingon, and so I’m back to analysing him and his textual development: this time, how his stance towards leaving Valinor and going to Beleriand developed over the decades-long textual history.
We know Fingon as the prince who opposed his father in wanting to remain in Valinor, implicitly agreeing with Fëanor, who recklessly jumped in at Alqualondë to defend the Fëanorians, and who had loved Maedhros once and for this reason decided to try to do what Maedhros’s brothers hadn’t dared and save his life.

summary:
Many ages ago, before the memory of all we speak of, perhaps before the Years of the Sun, there was a Ring unlike any other.
It was said that Melkor Lord of Fire fell from grace and was thrust from Arda, but what was not said is that he forged a Ring like that of his servant Sauron, and that this Ring had the power to raise not only Melkor, but any fallen being from the dead.
And there were other things left unsaid: that the Ring was taken from Melkor and called Reena-domë. That it could only be destroyed by casting it into the Secret Fire. That it would come to a hobbit-maid and be taken to save a man who felt he did not deserve salvation.
The will of Ilúvatar is clear: the Ring must be destroyed, and the siege of Minas Tirith must end. A new Fellowship forms to carry out these tasks, but one thing holds them back: the trust that Aragorn, the prophesied king of Gondor, cannot place in himself. A single choice on his part may prove to be Middle-earth's salvation or its doom, and one prophecy after another seems to suggest that, because of him, all is lost.
But there is hope yet, for destiny is not something to be found, but made, and there are some things that cannot be broken.

summary:
Believing he is still banished, Bilbo Baggins, injured, grief-stricken, and heartsick, leaves Erebor without a word, being escorted home by Gandalf, along with King Thranduil and his son.
That plan, however, gets thrown out the window when Bilbo discovers that his mithril shirt is not the only gift from Thorin that he left the Lonely Mountain with. Any semblance of normalcy in Bilbo's life swiftly follows when, on the day of his son's birth, he discovers that the gorgeous green stone he unearthed in his personal garden was, in fact, not a stone at all, but rather a dragon egg that had been lying dormant beneath the earth for thousands of years.
Bilbo's life becomes filled with joy again as he raises the most peculiar set of twin boys that have ever graced Middle-earth, but having such a source of old, powerful magic around a Ring of Power is dangerous. Evil things begin to stir across the land, and Bilbo finds himself thrust on another wild adventure, this time with a gaggle of faunts in tow.

summary:
Finrod Felagund is *interesting*. He’s often seen as this saintly wonderful creature of love and goodness, but he is in fact a Finwean even if his mother is from Alqualondë and his father tried very hard to pretend that he wasn’t related to his two quarrelsome brothers, and his character is greyer than often assumed.
The point of this is not to argue that Finrod is a villain, or that his many good qualities don’t exist. Instead, I want to explore his darker, more questionable traits and choices. Because he *is* a Finwean, and he *has* flaws, just like everyone else in this disaster of an extended family.

summary:
"Éomer, son of Éomund and Third Marshal of the Mark, did not have time for women or relationships. That had always been the case. He’d been on this path for many years, one of being a Knight of Rohan, putting his country first through his service. It never left any time for courting any of the women of Edoras. He told himself over and over again that he didn’t have the time for that; courting was a luxury he couldn’t afford himself.
He’d seen other men catch feelings, and he certainly understood the phrasing of that. To him, it always looked like they caught some sort of incurable illness. Feelings were a disease in Éomer’s mind. One that made a man way worse for wear in war. So he simply couldn’t afford that in these days of war.
Éomer was pretty good at balancing all of that, at making sure he didn’t get too close to anyone he thought would be interested in him, and he definitely wasn’t about to catch feelings for anyone any time soon.
So how was it that Boromir, son of Denethor, mighty warrior of Gondor, slipped past his awareness?"
----

summary:
He should be happy that he earned everything he wanted in the end. His brother returning alive to him, Middle Earth saved from a grave threat, the King returning and Gondor restored to its former glory. He lost many friends but made new ones. It’s the best ending he could ask for, and yet…
He was not happy.
The wounds are healing but they still ache. The things he locked away in a carefully crafted compartment burst free. In the quiet brought by peace, the noise inside his head grew loud. Now there was more time to think about the complexities of his relationships, to absorb the shock of his father’s deeds throughout his life.
The sin weighed heavy in his heart, sealed tight with the oath of silence he swore to his Lord. It’s getting harder and harder to keep up with the façade, to ignore the tremors, the flightiness, the fatigue, the anxiety.

title: Holly, Nettles, and Other Uncomfortable Things
author: RiaSaun
fandoms: The Lord of the Rings - J. R. R. Tolkien
summary:
Aegnor of Eregion greeted him. “Lord Glorfindel, you can see that we cannot have these Avari here when Lord Celeborn arrives.”
“Lord Elrond would never turn away people who needed his help, even Wild Elves like these.” Anidhren’s fingers twisted in her hair revealed her discomfort, but her voice rang clear and firm.
By the looks on their faces, the scorn in her final words struck more deeply with the Rivendell elves than the hospitality of her first; a sullen mutter from among the Avari suggested that they heard it the same way.
A woman he hadn’t noticed kneeling at the fore of the Avari shot to her feet. Loose wisps of dark hair unraveled around her narrow, sunbrowned face. Her low, burred voice prickled like a thousand nettles, and then he recognized her, and recognized why he’d felt such a sense of impending doom. The hackles on the back of his neck did not need the experience of ages to confirm that this would be trouble, that she would bring trouble.This is the seed of a prickly love story for Glorfindel, started to answer Lady Garavmithiel's "Love for the Lord" challenge; now restarted. Thanks for reading!

fandoms: The Hobbit - J. R. R. Tolkien

summary:
While the Fellowship fought for the Ring at the Black Gate of Mordor, over in Greenwood, another battle was waging under the leaves. What happened? What was the outcome? Will they ever recover? The aftermath was horrific, with many dead and even more injured. The battlefield was bad, but the camp was worse. Many more died after the battle had finished. Slowly drowning in guilt, and with nothing he can do to change the outcome, how will he deal with the weight dragging him down? Was all the suffering worth it? Nothing he can say will fix anything, but maybe there is something he can do to make it better. Maybe there is hope out there. Maybe it wasn't in vain.
Or...
Aftermath of the battle in Greenwood after the ring was destroyed (hence the name), and ultimately the toll the years of war had on the forest, and its people, but more specifically, its King. Also, there may or may not be another thing that is determined to destroy everything Thranduil loves, and it's up to Elrond to figure it out :)

summary:
There’s been a lot of discussion recently about the Doom and about how Beren, Thingol, Dior and Elwing were justified in wanting/keeping the Silmaril, because it eventually led to Eärendil managing to get through the barriers that the Valar had erected around Valinor to keep that pesky, inconvenient war out and convincing the Valar to do their jobs.

There is no indication whatsoever that Beren, Thingol, Dior and Elwing thought that keeping the Silmaril was necessary to fulfil some Doom and to save the world from Morgoth; instead, it’s clear that they all coveted the Silmaril at least in part for inherently selfish reasons.

Tyelkormo looked at him but said nothing.
Carnistir narrowed his gaze at Tyelkormo. “You know something.”

That was the problem, always.
Atarinkë could lie to his father with angelic sincerity. He could lie to Macalaurë while crying convincingly enough to earn hugs afterward. He had once lied directly to Carnistir’s face.

summary:
Before the Sun. Before anyone in Middle-earth has ever needed the word "war."
A man from our world wakes up as one of the first elves who ever lived.
No system. What he has is messier than any of that. A head full of knowledge about a world that hasn't been built yet, and the memory of every terrible thing coming for the people sleeping around him.
He can't stop all of it. He's honest enough to admit that.
Some of it, though? Maybe.
But that comes later. First there's the small problem of building a nation out of nothing.
That's the story. Not the war waiting at the end of it, but the work that comes first. The slow, stubborn, sometimes impossible task of taking a handful of elves who looked the gods in the eye and said no, and making a civilization out of them.

Her father! Her dear, dear world of a father. As ineluctable as the seasons and as unknowable. She was made in his likeness. They were a mirror and its reflection, spiralling on for eternity. summary:
Wualuna is a Maia born straight from the Music of the Ainur, drifting into existence not in the light of Valinor but in the broken shadowlands outside Angband. Drawn to a dissonant sorrow she cannot yet name, she wanders into the Black Foe's domain and finds Melkor upon his throne. To her, he is not a tyrant or a fallen god. He is simply someone who sounds… hurt. What begins as curiosity becomes quiet companionship: a childlike Maia humming fragments of the original Music into iron halls that were never meant to hold anything gentle. But harmony does not heal dissonance, and she, who understands only music and balance, slowly learns that not everything broken can be repaired. When Melkor is cast into the Void, something inside her fractures for the first time. It is grief, sharp and unfamiliar.
In time, she leaves Aman and becomes a wandering presence in Middle-earth: a soft echo at the edges of despair, a quiet comfort in places where hope is thin.But even after the ending of the Third Age and her return West, beyond the Doors of Night, where Melkor was cast, she sits and sings into the endless Void..
Waiting, still believing that somewhere beyond it, the one she once called "friend" might one day answer.

summary:
This story about Adar and an original character is not built upon a conventional romantic arc, but arises from the deepest questions of human Being and Existence. It speaks of questions to which many find no answers: what Home truly means, whether beauty can be found beneath ruins, Home within loss of Belonging, and Understanding within a world of Misunderstanding.
How does one decide after seeking these in vain throughout an entire lifetime - a Starfleet officer who, through her Force-sensitivity, is now “alone” in the universe, and capable of something that may not be accidental. How does she come to Middle-earth, and how do her missions intertwine with the fundamental questions of her existence. The story places humanity’s deepest frailties under examination, primarily in relation to non-human beings - not to show what we are, but what we might become.
Ambassador Sarah Lincoln pursues the greatest evil, as a new mission irrevocably alters her life. With a Jedi soul and Starfleet ideals, she attempts to achieve something extraordinary in Middle-earth, where a bond unfolds between her and Adar that becomes destiny-shaping not merely as a romantic promise, but as an experience lived at the level of Being.

You had loved Elrond all of your life.You had loved him when you were young and the world still felt new. When the sunlight was blessed and your toes on the grass were worth lingering over for minutes. Hours.You had loved him when horrors had ruled. summary: For me, the most intriguing thing about Beren and Lúthien’s story has always been a vague feeling that it does not belong in the Quenta. It took me a while to understand why: Beren and Lúthien is a fairytale dropped into the middle of an epic tragedy. These two literary genres are diametrically opposed and follow entirely different genre conventions and tropes, and that is why Beren and Lúthien has always felt so jarring to me in the wider context of the Quenta, and why Lúthien herself feels like a Mary Sue.

summary:
Fool of a Took seemed to be the enduring muttered mantra of the Fellowship, at least where Gandalf was concerned. It was entirely possible that the others thought it in their hearts– certainly not his fellow hobbits, but perhaps the Men that were sworn to follow Frodo into fire and flames, the grumbling dwarf, and the strange elf who spoke rarely and blinked even less. Pippin tried not to let it prick his heart: he knew this quest was something far beyond his understanding of the world, knew that truly realizing it would warp his brain in ways that could not be undone, knew that, after all, he was just a simple hobbit who had quite literally stumbled into saving the world. He could quell the pinpricks with those thoughts.
Before Moria, of course. Before knocking the helmet down the well. Before the balrog. 
(In which Legolas has a bad time, Pippin has even worse time, and the Fellowship finally gets around to talking about the balrog incident, though not before Legolas and Pippin run into trouble in the woods.)

summary:
Eamund is the name she is given, and it is the only thing she knows when she wakes up to the smell of smoke. The name sounds both unfamiliar on her tongue and yet inherently her own. Her heart accepts this name as a gift from the Valar, though her mind fights it. The Valar? Her eyes scrunch further closed. Why would she think of anything as a gift from the Valar?
Saved from the smoking village she deduces must be her home, she is taken to Meduseld where she is given the task of caring for Rohan's most prized possession: its young prince, recently orphaned from his mother. As she grows to love him, she must learn to protect him in any way that she can. One attack on the prince can be a thoughtless attempt, but two is a plot. Who wants Théodred dead? Why is Prince Théoden, his father, seeking her out so often? And why is everything both familiar and not?

summary: Callan MacRae wanted a quiet life. After years of proving himself as a Ranger—fighting old prejudice reawakened by his Pictish blood—he had finally earned a peaceful post in the southern fiefs. Solitude, stillness, and the rhythm of a life spent in service to his king and kingdom. That was enough.Unfortunately, life had other plans.Waking in a foreign land with no sign of Araluen, Callan finds himself thrust into the heart of Rohan—a kingdom of horse-lords, wary glances, and daggers hidden in the dark. With little more than his training and grit to rely on, he means to keep his distance. But when the royal court mistakes him for one of the Dúnedain of the North, he is pulled into their world more deeply than intended.As bonds form and trust begins to grow, Callan finds something unexpected: a sense of belonging, and the quiet pull of affection for a certain warrior poet. But old wounds fester, and when Callan begins to see too much of his own people in the Dunlendings the court so despises, tensions rise and loyalties are tested.

"He’s the finest specimen of a Longbeard I’ve seen in three centuries," Bifur grunted, signing the words with a look of genuine awe.
"It’s a problem, is what it is," Dwalin growled, crossing his massive arms as he watched the scene across the hall.
At least five Dwarves,sons and daughters of noble houses,were currently surrounding Gimli’s table. One was offering a finely wrought silver brooch; another was reciting a poem about the durability of granite; a third was trying to catch his eye with a display of masterfully tempered daggers.
By all accounts, Gimli should have been the proudest Dwarf in the Mountain. Instead, he looked as though he were chewing on a lemon.
....
........
..........
.....
there was a blur of movement,a whistle of wind and the distinct clack of a bow being drawn.
The music died. The laughter cut out into a jagged silence.
Legolas was suddenly standing at Gimli’s side. His bow was up, the string pulled taut against his cheek, and the gleaming tip of a Mirkwood arrow was leveled directly at the center of the Dwarven lady’s forehead.

And so, the hobbit left for the Shire, Gandalf and a horse in tow. This is where his story ends.But–wait. I’m terribly sorry. That cannot be it, can it? Ocbo, a Uruk-hai chieftain of the Iron Hide Horde, is carved from conquest and command. His world is strength, obedience, and endless war. That cadence breaks when a raid on a human village unearths Kierna, a woman who refuses to run and instead fights. Her defiance should mean death, but it captivates him. He claims her under his protection, meant to sate the hunger she stirs within him. But proximity becomes a battlefield, and possession turns into devotion.
Kierna is no ordinary human. Under pressure and conflict, her power awakens. She sees the threads binding all living things, and can sever them with terrifying clarity. But magic like hers is never simple, nor is her new world.
Through war and uneasy alliance, the orc/human couple forge something neither can name. Not softness. Not peace. Something harder. Truer. Their union turns volatile and rare. Children are born of it, power awakens within them, and war shifts around their family. summary: "Very few at the funeral understood any of that. "I am just a traveler," Aurora says. It’s not a lie, but it isn't the whole truth.
In Skyrim, the moons were her constant companions. In Middle-earth, the sky is a hollow, alien vault where Masser and Secunda are nowhere to be found. Stranded in the Riddermark with only a steel blade, dagger and a heavy cloak, Aurora is a woman out of time and space, struggling to navigate the social intricacies of Arda while mourning a home that feels like a fading dream.
She tries to blend in with Aragorn’s company, but when you carry the soul of a dragon, "blending in" is a losing game. She knows nothing of the local customs, the history, or the darkness rising in the East—she doesn't even know what an "Uruk-hai" is. But she knows how to fight, she knows how to survive, and under the watchful eye of a curious Wizard, she’s about to find out that some secrets are impossible to keep when the drums of war begin to beat.

summary:
"The people are fools!" Denethor whirled around, his eyes bright with a frantic, desperate light. "You are my son. My heir. The blood of Westernesse is pure in you. You were taught that the word of the Steward is law. Do you deny your blood? Do you deny your father?"
Boromir flinched. The weight of his upbringing was a physical thing, a mountain of expectation he had climbed every day of his life. Denethor had shaped him, molded him into the shield of Gondor, and for forty years, Boromir had never known a world where his father’s word was not the absolute truth.
"I do not deny you, Father," Boromir whispered.
"Then prove it." Denethor stepped forward, placing a tray into Boromir’s shaking hands. On it sat a delicate porcelain pot and a single cup. The steam rising from it smelled faintly of mountain herbs and something sharper,something bitter. "The 'King' is weary from his paperwork. He sits in his solar, vulnerable. Bring him this tea. Let the line of Stewards be restored before the sun sets."

summary:
Elrond frowned and tilted his head: at the very end of the table, the last gift to arrive, laid a small chest forged entirely in silver. An exquisite, if inexplicable gift. There were no seal and no letter accompanying it. Camnir had probably forgotten to include it: all the other gifts had a letter attached, full of solicitude and advice on lordly duties. Elrond lifted the chest, raising it to his curious eyes, turning it around to examine it. The chest was covered in foliage engraving, very faint, barely visible, but noticeable under his fingers. On the bottom, he thought he could guess at the engraving of a tree. What realm could that be? Whose lord was it? As he looked at the bottom, the lid opened, no lock protecting its content, and the gift inside spilled out on his fingers.
After the siege of Ost-in-Edhil, a new palace for the Elves is built, a stronghold against the rising darkness. Elrond Peredhel, the new lord, soon realises that darkness is not done with him yet.

“You are not fighting me,” he said, quieter now, studying Elrond’s face.
“I said—” Elrond swallowed, the movement caught under Thranduil’s hand, and the sensation sent another visible shudder through him. His fingers closed harder around the wrist he held, somehow doing more to anchor it in place than get rid of it. “Release me.”
The command lacked its force. Thranduil’s eyes flicked down to the hand gripping his wrist, then back to Elrond’s face, taking in the flush rising along his cheekbones, the uneven breath, the tension that looked nothing like fear. Something like surprise—real surprise—crossed the Elvenking’s face.
“This is...” he murmured, almost to himself, “unexpected.”

summary:
After being killed by his children, Adar awakens — whole and uninjured — in an unfamiliar forest. As he struggles to understand what has happened to him or how he came to be in this strange place, he hears distant footsteps and spots a human woman walking straight toward him. Hidden behind a large tree, he watches her in stunned fascination, immediately captivated by her almost elven beauty and the quiet, graceful aura that surrounds her.
When she finally notices the tall, imposing Uruk — his piercing blue eyes gleaming beneath dark armour, standing only a few steps away, half veiled by the forest’s twilight — she panics. Shocked, she turns and runs, screaming as she flees for her life. She barely makes it a few steps before he is already behind her, silencing her with a hand over her mouth and pulling her firmly against him.
What follows seems inevitable. As he commands her to be quiet — his hot breath brushing her ear, their bodies pressed so tightly together it feels as though fate itself placed them in each other’s arms — something ancient stirs, setting everything in motion.

Gimli spotted Tauriel from time to time, though he’d never spoken to her. He’d no wish to. He’d resented her presence for so long, glaring every time he saw her, biting back the urge to shout at her to go away, to leave his people be. He’d been furious every time he saw her at Kíli’s grave; it felt like she was stealing his time with his kin, for he could not even visit Fíli or Thorin while she was with Kíli. Not comfortably. He couldn’t talk to them with her there, so he always stormed off in anger and waited for her to leave. He was always happy to see the back of her.
Until now, until now that he finally understood. Now he was sorry to have missed her.

tags: Canon Divergence - The Lord of the Rings
summary:
Note: A reliquary is a container made to hold, protect, and display sacred relics/objects. The relic in this story happens to be pure evil.
This is a first-person story, as told by hardboiled Auror Harry Potter. It is written in a style reminiscent of graphic detective writers such as Dashiell Hammett, Mickey Spillane, and Frank Miller, among others. It would translate into a 40s-50s film noir.
Harry is bored, in need of some action. It comes to him in the form of the story's femme fatale, Pansy Parkinson. She is desperate to find help locating an ancient relic purported to possess extremely dangerous evil powers. and for someone to save her from possible death at the hands of others seeking it. Harry reluctantly decides to help her. But before long, he realises he is involved in something far more dangerous than he signed on for.
For LOTR fans, the crossover comes in late, but is crucial to the resolution of the story, because the world of Harry Potter does not include demons. The closest thing to them is dementors. That means the story needs a little outside help. With the assistance of Hermione, a pair of wizards from LOTR are identified to enter the story and aid in the final resolution.

Adar looked him over slowly, eyes coming back to meet his, “Very well,” he said, he sounded disappointed.

He was silent for a moment. She heard his cloak rustle, the sound of his hand grasp one of the bars. The gentle tap of his rings against the metal filled her ears, and she shut her eyes.
“When you denied an alliance with me, I found other means of quenching my thirst.”
“For violence and depravity?” she shot back.
“For vengeance,” he hissed. “Just as you sought yours. Keep your righteousness to yourself. I care not for it. These Men, these Númenóreans, fought against me in the Great War. Slew countless lives. With their pride and their arrogance in their mighty goodness. They thought they were better than the rest of us as you yourself believed you were better than me.” His voice dropped to a whisper. “I wanted to see them suffer. I have achieved so much more than that.”

Yet amidst the desolation and the exquisite agony of the Ring's burden, I find my mind returning back to Sam. My dear Sam.
My most beloved friend. This journey would be fraught without him. His courage—his selflessness; they exist in no small sum.
Words fail me now—my tongue sits heavy, scorned by fatigue and the malice that eats at me in this place. Mordor hungers for a sacrifice, preying on what was left of our merriment. I see how it eats at him—the weariness in his tired gaze. Yet each time we find our blades clashing with the steel of danger, the dullness awakens to a clarity so sharp I could hardly withstand its ferocity. Purpose.
Our rations have nearly dwindled to nothing, yet he never wavers. He starves so that I do not. He persists when I can hardly imagine it so. Nary a hesitation, nor a singular dissidence.
I pray Sam knows how precious he is to me. His mere presence soothes the ache in my heart—the drain of the Ring and its insistence to return to its master.
***
I cannot lie and swear I am a man unsoiled—the seduction of reprieve amidst this misery—corruption—calls to me. But when I look to him... I find the strength to take another step.

summary:
In the second age, in the far South and East of Middle-Earth, beyond the maps that kings and elves have named, Sauron does not return in thunder - he returns in administration. Treaties sealed in spice, oaths weighed against water, and alliances bought with the promise of order. In the uncharted desert, he gathers factions to him one careful concession at a time - learning from another old darkness in a fairer mask - reading fears, planting needs, training loyalty until it feels like choice. Sauron in his Halbrand form offers continuity to councils and works his way toward the throne not as a conqueror but as a solution. There are moments, dangerously human, when he almost believes the mask.
Pre Season 2 Rings of Power. Dune AU.Thanks for reading! Tolkien leaves the South and East fairly open, so I'm using that space to place Arrakis and the city of Arrakeen as a believable civilisation. Some Dune elements are reimagined to fit middle earth, while keeping the second age timeline and stakes in view.

summary: The Endless Ache: what was and what comes to be of Boromir and Sedryneth’s love. Starting with their courtship, this story is a glimpse at a young Boromir — newly promoted Captain of Gondor — and his rebellious nature toward his stubborn and abrasive father. Frolicking around the city with a nobleman’s daughter, dipping behind the white walls to steal a kiss occupies his time instead of training to be a strong and skilled warrior. Despite his father’s hesitance toward his son marrying, he agrees to arrange a union between the two young Gondorians not out of the grace of his own heart, but out of selfishness as he felt he may benefit from it. Years pass and the distinguished Captain of Gondor has a new title; da. Sedryneth gives her love the gift of fatherhood not once but three times. And when Boromir goes to run an errand in Rivendell for his father, he leaves behind a fairly pregnant wife anxiously waiting for his return. News comes from the company of Rangers patrolling the shores of Osgiliath: Boromir has died. Sedryneth is driven to madness, grief weighing on her psyche as time passes. How does one continue on for her children when their father has left this realm? The roots of her very being have been ripped from her.

He was the warden of the golden wood, sworn to its silence and its borders.She was a child of the forest, untamed and unbound, her spirit carried on the wind.He was measured; she was wild.He was stone; she was sunlight.He was a shield; she was the song it guarded.

summary:
If they are not human, than what exactly are they?
This question has been running through Lily's mind ever since she found herself stuck with these strange fae inhabiting her house. After various events, she has slowly given up hope on getting away from them, but that does not mean that she cannot help other people in the future. With the interest of humanity at heart (and definitely not to fight off her boredom) Lily sets out to create a journal documenting the fae with their habits, but also their weaknesses and strengths. Unfortunately it is rather difficult to experiment on creatures who do no speak your language and are almost twice your size. Still, Lily tries even if she herself has no clue what exactly is going, and if that means risking the wrath of her captors by ending up stuck on the roof after a failed experiment or 'accidentally' lighting one of them on fire to see if they are fire proof, then so be it.
This work can be read as a standalone but I recommend you read the first part of this series, Andorotaurë, first to properly understand the context.

Fíli Durin is trying his hardest to honour his chronically stressed uncle's sacrifices and take some of the weight of managing Orc Pit from his hands. Following a desperate flight through the heavy woods, she collapses within the domain of Beorn the skin-changer. He is a massive guardian of the wild who has seen his own people slaughtered. But suddenly, he felt it.
A warm, almost blinding light suddenly filling his senses. Making him hiss in pain, his level of agony rising until it slowly twisted itself into pleasure. A subconsciousness was now nestled against his own, he wasn’t sure of how long it has been there, nor of the time that passed before it came.
Days? Months? Years? Perhaps even centuries of nothingness. But he curiously nudged it, his liquid form almost buzzing with anticipation as he waited. And eventually, it nudged back. Curious and tentative, but almost playful in a way.
He nudged it again, reaching for it as he found himself wanting - yearning to know more. But the subconscious backed away, dissipating, leaving him alone once more. He found himself growing for contact, aching for it. For the subconscious to come back, for her to come back.

The One Ring was destroyed, but the power within it remained. It was distributed among the remaining rings, growing stronger with the destruction of each successive vessel. summary:
The children of Aragorn Elessar and Arwen Undómiel vanished on the very night when darkness besieged the city. An ancient and potent light, sudden and without warning, struck them and cast them far back into the past, to a time before the War of the Ring had even begun. None among them knows what befell them, nor that the others endured the same fate.
They were sent forth to guide those who would shape the future: to forestall impending dangers, to safeguard that which must endure, and to share their knowledge. Their mission is clear: guide and tell. To protect those destined to survive and to die, to illuminate the uncertain, and to buy precious time for the world.
Yet so long as they remain scattered, the curse holds them fast, and none recall that they ever existed.
One awakens beneath a luminous canopy, where leaves glisten like gold. Another treads across plains swept by an ancient wind, whispering forgotten tales. The third finds shelter amidst tranquil hills and discreet inhabitants. The last walks alongside a man whose destiny remains yet veiled.
A long journey is awaiting them.

summary:
“ 'Héra, sometimes people fight…sometimes, sadly, arguments cannot be settled with words. Sometimes people must defend those they love.'
Olwyn observed the child’s reactions, keeping eye contact with her, as she spoke. She chose her words carefully; she was well acquainted with the child’s tendency to fall into worries and ruminations, even at her tender age.
Yet Héra’s eyes widened and her mouth hung open just the slightest bit. Her attention was happily fixed. Yes, the girl was one to deeply feel…yet Olwyn wasn’t surprised to see her – as fearless and precocious as could be – seeming intrigued rather than afraid at this particular story. She was a bold one, and a warrior’s spirit ran in her blood.
'And here’s what I actually like about that, as unfortunate as it can be…sometimes the people who do that are women. Women like you will be! We call them Shieldmaidens.'
She took another breath. Héra’s lagoon-green eyes were even wider. She leaned in towards Olwyn in rapt anticipation."

[Giving him his space, Sam quietly replied, “Let me help you,” the support flowing easily from his tongue.
When Frodo shook his head, it wasn’t to deny help. Instead, he meant that he could not, for Frodo had come to understand that there was nothing to be done. In the time since he’d awoken with the ring finally gone, he had tried to regain what it had taken from him. He did all the hobbies he used to, he tried new experiences, he talked and drank and laughed. None of it felt quite right, nor did anything fill the hollowness in his bones. Even in certain peace, he could not calm. He did not seem to belong in his home, in the Shire, or anywhere at all. Something had broken and changed within him so severely and so out of reach, and not even Sam could hope to fix that. Every day solidified that belief further.
But Sam didn’t catch on, misinterpreting his meaning. “I want to help,” he said, as if Frodo simply had to let him in and it would be alright.
“I know, Sam.”]

THIS WHOLE THING IS A DRAFT
Story of my Tolkien Universe OC (Cyneowe). It contains an original language, original locations, original storyline and original characters.
Cyne is a young woman born in Danminhar, with a loving family and a husband that she keps close to her heart. But then she decided that it is time for her to create her own path and follow her dreams to defend her people. That is how she ends up in a small group of women (and few men) with that same objective. She goes from being a dreamer to accept her people's tragic fate, and her own. But even if her life did not go the way she planned, she gets her own kind of peaceful, happy ending with the love of her life and free of guilt. summary:
The final blessings of colour splash Thranduil’s moon-pale skin with shades of lilac. Streaks of fuchsia illuminate his hair and dusky rose washes over his fine olive-gray silk robes. It’s an intimate and ethereal show of beauty that threatens to steal Elrond’s breath, and effectively puts all other sunsets to shame.
Admittedly, every sunset spent in the company of Thranduil has a habit of putting all the sunsets that came before it to shame. It’s an ongoing problem.
A lick of heat crawls up Elrond’s neck as he catches himself staring and he quickly diverts his attention to topping up his own goblet. Scrabbling for the threads of their conversation, he berates himself as he so often has in the more than ten-hundred years that he has called Thranduil friend, that he may as well be lusting after Ilúvatar for all his longing will amount to anything more.

summary:
Casey O’Connell doesn't do "adventure." She does inventory.
As the night manager of a South Boston gas station, Casey’s life consists of broken slushie machines, aggressive customers, and a crushing amount of student debt. She doesn't hike, she doesn't believe in magic, and the last time she saw a forest was on a postcard.
But when a slip in the rain sends her tumbling through the cracks of reality, she doesn't land in the ER. She lands in freezing white water, dodging black arrows and drowning alongside dwarves in barrels.
Dragged dripping wet and furious before the Elven King Thranduil (who looks like a supermodel with a god complex) Casey has no idea where she is or why everyone has pointy ears. She only knows that she is cold, terrified, and absolutely not going in a cell.
Thranduil finds her rude, messy, and baffling. She finds him arrogant and impossible.
He offers her the dungeon. She demands dinner. And just like that, the fate of the Woodland Realm gets a little more complicated.

Of their daughter, first and foremost, but also of what had once forced her to flee from the shores of the Middle-earth, leaving behind all the ones she loved. For even after all those long centuries, for all the skills of the Valar and the soothing, lulling peace of Aman, a cruel seed of illness still laid deep within her, a clump of ice between her ribs, that never fully went away, forgotten in her happiest moments, but still lying under, ready to resurface.

Note: English is not my first language.
This story is inspired by the series The Rings of Power.
In the beginning, there was only the light... pure, ancient, and unbroken. Yet where light shines, shadows always follow, waiting in silence for their moment to return.
They met in the stillness between duty and dawn - when the world was quiet enough for hearts to speak. She wore the light of her lineage like armor, golden and untouchable, yet her eyes sought the truth beyond the walls of her father's throne. He was the herald, sworn to carry the words of kings, not the whispers of his own soul. But when their gazes met, the air itself seemed to tremble - as if creation remembered the sound of its first heartbeat.
Their love was a secret woven between shadows, fragile as morning mist and fierce as the flame that shapes steel. The world would have called it betrayal, but to them it was salvation, the one place where duty could not reach and silence could not reign.
And though they knew the dawn would break them apart, still they chose to stand in that forbidden light, even for a single heartbeat more.

Long before the darkness of Mordor, there was light and love. Kalsar was once an Elf of rare gentleness: a poet and scholar who came to Middle-earth not to conquer, but to to capture the essence of it. To archive and preserve it's stories.
In the green haven of Lithadorel, he and his beloved Pinc-tywyll built a sanctuary for lost and orphaned souls, a sanctuary granted after years of service to the high king. But love that defies the passing of ages demands a price and very time Kalsar swears to protect his wife, he draws closer to the shadow that will one day consume him.

summary:
Hands caught her lower back, just barely keeping her on her feet. “Forgive me ser, I did not see–” only to look up into the deep blue eyes of an elf.
“There is nothing to forgive,” he said, his voice was a gentle creek in the thunderstorm of her heart. He took a step back and she immediately missed his warmth. “My lady, I am Legolas of the Woodland Realm,” he pressed his hand to his chest with a slight bow, “it is a pleasure to meet you.”
“Oh, yes. Thank you,” she gave her name with a slight curtsy, “but I am not a lady, I’m just a rider. And leaving.” She shifted on her toes, “my aid was not wanted here, and I shall not tarry here when I am at least allowed to protect my people back at home.” She moved to grab her saddle, but Legolas was faster, his hands brushed hers as she reached for the saddle. “My lord?”
“Forgive me, I did not ask–” he cleared his throat gently, “may I help you?”
“I would like that,” her face warmed, “thank you,” she added quickly.
“It’s my pleasure.” She took a moment to watch him as she set the bridle on her horse, he murmured to her horse and set her saddle, his long blonde hair lay loose down his back...For how slight his frame, he’s quite strong.

A year has passed since Legolas and Elrohir were wed beneath Greenwood’s leaves, their love steady as light through the trees. Peace has lingered, fragile and golden, but peace seldom lasts.
When autumn deepens, they journey west beyond the forest, seeking quiet roads and the simple beauty of the mortal world. Yet the land feels changed, heavy with silence. In a small village wrapped in mist, whispers rise of seregrog, blood spirits said to descend from Thuringwethil’s brood, thought long vanished from the world.
What begins as unease becomes fear, and fear becomes truth. Something walks by night, unseen but watching, drawn to light, and to love that burns too brightly.
Together, Elrohir and Legolas must face what lingers in the dark, where desire and death entwine, and the line between beauty and horror blurs. For where the light falters, shadows remember, and evil waits to be named again.

summary: "Then your power is too weak." Fëanor returned to his mithril, dismissing the argument. "If you cannot overcome the natural resistance of stone, you need more practice. Discipline. Hours of work until the magic answers as readily as my hammer does."Amras looked down at his hands—the same hands that had traced maps with Amrod, that had finally found purpose after centuries of drifting. He thought of the marsh, of sinking into drowning sleep, of awakening transformed. He remembered the mages' faces as they recognized what he'd become: Keeper of the Living Stone, they'd called him. The first of his bloodline to manifest such power. Something rare. Something precious.Something his father viewed as a problem to be solved through traditional jeweler's training.—This work takes place in the time after the great remaking of Arda,in Aman,after all the diseased elves have left Mandos’s Halls, were resurrected and are now free to walk in Valinor once again.—The topic of elves having magical abilities is explored much broader than in Tolkien’s canonical works—in my interpretation aside from elves with minor magical powers like Galadriel,also exist elf-mages who are intervened with magic deeply.

summary: Éodred was never meant to be a hero. Disguised as the young man “Kai,” she joined the Fellowship to save her father—not to fight Sauron’s war. Rejected by some and mistrusted by others, she must now earn back the comradeship she never expected to value… and reconcile with the woman she’s become.Beside her stands Boromir—proud, wounded, and quietly unraveling after the breaking of the Fellowship. There they both stood, and there, in the deepening dusk and in the settling night, two heavy and sorrowful hearts met. It was all too late. Before them only the great abyss stretched unending.Shadows fall and darkness stretches over Middle-Earth, its reach growing longer still. The Free People face enemies not only in the open; hidden and secret, the great Enemy knows well to break their spirit, their will to fight, long before his armies come forward. The walls of Minas Tirith stand tall, strong, yet the strength of Men wanes. Trouble brews over the plains of Rohan, and the horse-masters remain ever vigilant in their watch. In the North, the Dunedain Rangers fight a war unseen by most; protecting lands that find themselves at an uncertain peace. But for how long?The Enemy is soon ready.A young woman sets out on a journey that will change her life forever.

summary:
The time of peace is over. The shadows of Mirkwood grow denser, and encounters with monsters become ever more frequent. The world begins to falter, and the finely balanced order of life is shaken.
This is the story of a ring - and of how a journey east came to mean rekindled love for the half-elf Lithil and the Elven Prince Legolas.An ancient friendship binds the two. Love at first sight that endured for an entire millennium. And yet fate had other plans than ever bringing them together.
Legolas became the prince one would wish for; Lithil, on the other hand, chose the path of a warrior, rising to commander and master of the blade.Guided by duty and oaths, the two became partners in life only. A friendship so deep and intimate that new feelings could destroy everything.

summary:
Erestor’s sword is black with blood. A wave crashes up the steps to the terrace as another orc barrels toward him. He jerks back, too slow to parry. A flash. Cold like a blade of winter drives into his face and neck. Something is wrong. His grip falters. His head drops back, refusing his command. All he sees is the sky and elves falling around him. The world’s noise thins to a strange ringing, as if submerged underwater. Then pain erupts, scorching from brow to cheek to throat. Warm liquid spills down his face, blinding his right eye. His knees buckle and he falls. Something sweeps him into darkness. Grey skies drift away, walls rise, and oblivion takes him.
The tale of Erestor, of what was lost to war and what stubbornly survived. His life began in the prosperous Eregion at the time of its prime. Yet when the War of Elves and Sauron started, his life came crashing down all at once. He fled into a world remade by grief and burdened with memories. The road led him to Imladris and to a new life of lesser splendour and hushed turmoil. As time passes, he will have to find peace again and learn how to survive his past. And perhaps, in the quiet, he will discover something he never dreamed would be his again.

In the golden twilight of Aragorn's wedding to Arwen, Idrial’s heart breaks quietly. Berethor was never hers—not truly. But when the ever-watchful eyes of Legolas Greenleaf catch her in sorrow, he steps in, first out of mischief, then with growing desire. What begins as a ruse—a mock-courtship for the eyes of others—unravels into something devastatingly real.
Their fake affection becomes a wildfire, burning in gardens, on balconies, in shadowed alcoves—tangled limbs, whispered elvish, domination laced with devotion. She submits; he commands. She blooms under his praise, and he devours her with aching hunger.
But Idrial cannot stay. Her vows to Galadriel hold her back, and Legolas, unwilling to dishonor her duty, lets her go.
Years pass. When they meet again, a child walks at her side, sunlight in his hair and stormlight in his eyes.
Now the King of the Woodland Realm, Legolas must fight for the woman who haunts his dreams, the child born of their passion, and the future still promised beneath the white tree.

summary:
From the private writings of Galadriel: "I thought I had found a man. Not a hero, not even a king - just a man. Flawed and raw and full of want. He wore his pain on the outside, the way I wore mine on the inside, and I mistook that for honesty. But it was not Halbrand who answered when I pressed my mouth to his, or whispered my doubts into his skin. It was Sauron.
  And yet...he was the first one to truly see me. He saw the fury I could never purge, the pride I never confessed, the hunger that curled in my belly like fire. I remember the weight of his body over mine; his breath against my ear; the way he said my name as if he had known it long before the world began. I remember wanting him, not despite what he was, but because of it. Because he matched something I have always carried and never dared name.

  They say light drives out the dark; I have lived long enough to know better.

  Light calls to darkness, as surely as darkness calls to light. He was drawn to my light, and I to his darkness. Somewhere, somehow, in between, we became fully known...and perhaps, even, fully loved."

Galadriel is fading. The world feels greyer with each passing day, her body betraying her in ways the doctors can name but not cure. Nights are the only hours left that feel alive, and one night, she gives herself over to them - hungry for anything that might burn through the numbness.
In the club’s shadows she meets him. A stranger whose gaze feels like a wound and a promise all at once. What begins as a reckless encounter coils into something stranger, darker - an intimacy that lingers long after the night ends.
But the city is bleeding. Girls are found in alleyways, their lives emptied out of them, and every thread of the case seems to draw her back to him. summary:
“我原先已安於從舊世界的灰燼中，搶救那些遺留下來的東西、重建那些已失去的，”凱勒布林博說。“但後來你來了，你的到來改變了一切。我們在如此短的時間內學到並成就了這麼多。我們確實創造了一個美麗的中土世界，它所面臨的考驗同樣值得。如果一定要說，阿門洲甚至不比它完美，因為它的美麗從未像我的家那樣經受過試煉。”“我們的家，”安納塔輕聲修正。凱勒布林博看了他一會兒。“我們的家，”他重複一遍，停頓了一下——“我很高興你選擇停留在這。”“我也是，”安納塔回答。
在奧斯特-因-埃德希爾的黃金歲月裏的一個夏末夜晚，安納塔和凱勒布林博就權力、野心、自由和寬恕進行了長時間的交談。在這一天晚上，他們共同的希望使他們比以往任何時候都更加緊密地聯繫在一起，也是那一天，他們危險的野心開始推動那些將使他們先分道揚鑣並終將摧毀彼此的計畫。

summary:
As darkness finally fell, the stars emerged—but they were not the stars Alfred knew from his studies of celestial navigation. These were brighter, closer somehow, arranged in constellations that matched no astronomical chart he had ever seen. And among them, low on the western horizon, shone a single light that was not a star at all—a steady, unwavering radiance that called to mind the descriptions of the Silmaril bound to the brow of Eärendil.
"Turn back," a voice murmured. "This path is not for you, Child of Men. Return to your own shores while you still may."
"No," Alfred shouted into the howling wind. "I will not turn back. Not until I find him."
"He is beyond your reaching," the voice replied, its tone neither cruel nor kind, simply stating a fact as immutable as the laws of nature. "The circles of your world and his no longer intersect. Such is the Gift of Ilúvatar to Men, and the Doom laid upon the Eldar."
"I reject that gift," Alfred cried, tears mingling with the rain on his face. "I reject that doom. There must be a way."

summary:
"Explain it to me," Boromir demanded. "This… filth in the shape of a poem. I know enough to know you have written something… bawdy. But I would hear its truth from you."
"No. Please," Faramir whimpered. "It is nonsense. A jest. A stupid, drunken—"
"I read the thing, Faramir. I could feel the lust curling the edges of the parchment. A drunken jest? No. This is meaningful. It's meticulous! Tell me what it means. Now."
"It means nothing!" Faramir choked out.
"Nothing, aye? Okay. 'Two-two was too satisfying'," Boromir read aloud. "Too much wetness. Hotness. And hardness." At the word hardness, he emphasised the point by crushing their bodies together, from head to toe. "What does it all mean? Shall I take it up to the scribes and ask for a court-wide workshop?"
Faramir's breath hitched. "You wouldn't."
"Try me," Boromir responded. "I've done worse for less, little brother."OR, the story of how Boromir finds Faramir's dirty little poem, gets intensely aroused by it, demands to know what and who it's about, and then is utterly unravelled by the answer.

What if the war for Middle-earth never happened? The Fellowship was never formed. The One Ring still lost to time.
As the Tree of Kings, the ancient power that binds the realms of Elves, Men and Dwarves, begins to mysteriously die, a long forgotten darkness stirs. Each leaf that falls from its branch weakens the barrier that holds creatures of shadow at bay.
As whispers of orcs and darker monsters return to the wild, Gandalf the Grey seeks the only power that might restore the balance—The Mirithen Stones; relics once wielded by the warriors of old. Warriors, like the late Queen of Mirkwood. In her absence, the fate of the world falls to her only son.
Unprepared and untested, Legolas has never set foot beyond the safety of his father’s forest. With no other choice, he is thrust into a broken world where a War of Races rages on, and nothing is as it seems.
With only a strange wizard to guide him and a growing magic he cannot yet control, Legolas must find the lost King of Gondor before the Tree of Kings withers away completely and darkness consumes them all.

But this time, desperation forces her first transformation into human form."Help me,"she whispers before losing consciousness, and Thranduil realizes the beloved wolf who once demanded belly rubs and saved his life is now a beautiful, traumatized woman struggling to speak, to trust, to exist in skin that feels foreign.As she learns human customs and battles PTSD, Thranduil finds himself torn between seeing her as the cherished pack member she's always been and the fierce, magnificent woman she's becoming. She may understand pack dynamics, but elvish court politics and his own growing desire are far more dangerous territories.Some bonds transcend species. summary:
In a world where Middle-earth and Earth have established diplomatic and academic relations, Alfred Pierson, a doctoral student at Harvard specialising in cultural trauma studies, finds himself unexpectedly hosted by Glorfindel, a legendary elven warrior and visiting professor from Imladris. What begins as a practical housing arrangement evolves into something deeper as they navigate cultural differences, academic challenges, and growing feelings for each other...
"I have wanted this," Glorfindel admitted softly, "for longer than I should confess."
"How long?" Alfred asked, his fingers still entwined in golden strands, marvelling at being permitted such intimacy.
A smile touched Glorfindel's lips—not the reserved expression Alfred was accustomed to, but something warmer, more open. "Since the night you fell asleep in the living room while reading that treatise on Sindarin dialectical variations. You had notes scattered around you, and your glasses had slipped down your nose. You looked... perfectly human, in the most beautiful way."

Valandil seemed to think for a moment, then get to his feet. 
'Yes, and what are we still doing in here?',"
~~~~
Anárion and Valandil led the way to an evening swim...one they weren't allowed to take, strictly speaking. Ontamo and Isildur had their own reasons to hesitate, but joined anyways. Eärien was more of an unwitting bystander ~ but ultimately joined in the fun. It became a memory they'd all hold for a long time.

Raised under a regime that warns her any use of her gift could cause harm, she chooses silence and restraint until a devastating betrayal forces her to question everything she was taught. As she uncovers the lies buried by those in power, she begins to see that the system she trusted may be built on fear and cruelty.

With themes of memory, control, and moral ambiguity, it follows one girl’s descent into power and the consequences of forcing a city to confront what it tried to forget. summary:
Drow. Dark Elves. Dökkálfar. All the same name for the sub-race of the Elves. Dark, evil, malicious - that's what they are known for. And it's true...for the most part. There is an exception in every race that breaks the stereotype. This just so happens to be such a story of a young man banished under a pretty mission of obtaining "glory".
Leif is a half-drow, born to a powerful mistress named Lolth. Raised to be the best assassin by her, he is sent away to the mainland of Middle Earth to earn the respect of his people and be able to return home as a somebody. However, Leif, for all his bloodthirst and streaks of cruelty, gets sucked into adventures and quests that change the world. He meets new people that chip away at his cold heart, who in their own ways (either knowingly or unknowingly) begin to make him question his place amongst the Dökkálfar and whether or not he wants to return to such a cruel place.
Over the course of his journeys Leif discovers that it isn't punished to help others, to be kind and to love. Leif, over his quest to find acceptance, finds himself with something greater than the hollow glory he was banished to find; friends, family...and love.

Samwise had loved Frodo for as long as he could remember, but at some point he had to grow up and acknowledge that love would never be returned.
Rosie, on the contrary, could return his love. She was the perfect woman: kind, beautiful, funny, caring. It was easy to love her, easy to fall into a comfortable life with her, easy to tell himself he was happier this way.
Then Frodo left, and he took a chunk of Sam’s heart with him.
It was a loss he didn’t feel allowed to mourn. So he didn’t, he carried on as usual, only he knew of the gaping hole that now existed within himself. He could still be happy, could be a good husband and father, could do everything he had always done even with that missing piece.
If only Frodo didn’t send that letter.

title: Of the Hero's Journey: A short essay on the merits of Peter Jackson's Frodo as a Hero.. Or Heroine?

fandoms: The Lord of the Rings - All Media Types
summary:
As a fan of PJ's trilogy as my entrypoint to all things Lord of The Rings, one of the aspects that have caught my attention the most since has been the difference in reception between Movie! Frodo and other characters of the cinematic adaptation. In particular because of how often his character is overlooked, or leveled complaints against under the notion of "having been watered down from the book." I don't intend to take those complaints at face value, and thus, I'm not responding to them, but the cultural context in which I believe they emerged. Therefore, my intent is to offer a shift in perspective, as well as more general, socially-oriented analysis, beyond the landscape of particular fandom disagreements and squabbles.
Welcome, my dear guests, to my hobbit hole as I elaborate in detail on Frodo's character in the movies, his reception, and the theoretical framework of Campbell's Heroic Journey and its limitations when it comes to analysing LOTR. Sigh. Yes, you can have some tea and explore the pantry. Be sure to get cozy for a short dissertation, whether you're Movie! Frodo fans, skeptics, or neutral on the whole matter. Let's begin!

tags: everyone share a single brain cell
summary:
Forget the songs of heroes. This is the real story of the Elves, as told by Caranthir, the only Noldo with a functioning brain cell and a ledger. While everyone else was busy making magic jewels, swearing dramatic oaths and charging Balrogs for fun, Caranthir was in the back muttering, "I told you so."
Watch him roast his family for their glorified suicides, facepalm as his brothers kidnap princesses and deliver a blistering post-mortem commentary from the Halls of Mandos. From the creation of the Silmarils ("You don’t just slam the door on a Vala!") to the fall of Sauron ("After all that… it was an accident?"), this is the ultimate tale of family dysfunction, catastrophic leadership and one grumpy elf who was right about everything. History's greatest tragedies have never been so hilariously frustrating.

"So tell me, Faramir-mine," Boromir said, voice thick with amusement, "is reading about the pleasures of the flesh the real reason you spend so much time in the library? And here I thought you were studying strategy. Silly me."
Faramir blinked. His fist clenched around the handle of his knife. "You went through my things," he said, tightly. "You are utterly insufferable."
"And you ought to be more careful," Boromir retorted, wiping his thumb along the corner of his mouth. "See, next time you spill yourself all over the archival velvet, someone less loving than me might find out. Imagine if our Lord Father Denethor found your… library paste… on the heritage fabrics? My, Faramir. What would he say?"
Faramir didn't know what their Father would say. But he did know it was time for revenge.OR, the story about an escalating, brotherly prank-war that quickly spirals out of control; involving forged letters regarding tree-fornication, staged wet-dreams, petty thievery, vanilla ice-cream used as psychosexual torture, and more.

summary:
Gondor is falling. Assailed from the east and the south while inside it rots, the White City will not hold for long. Corruption eats away at the pristine walls until the fissures make way for all sorts of vermin. Their whispers are foul, they spit curses and pray death; the eye is ever watchful.
Gondor has no king, and yet the steward reigns upon a throne of lies. He has forgotten his place, and now he tramples over the backs of his people. They have had enough, rebellion is brewing. The common folk will not stand for such trickery any longer, they will fight back.
From all borders, east to west, young and old are joining the revolution. Death to the steward, they preach, and may the throne's rightful heir storm the lands to claim his birthright. Gondor is sick of lies and sick of loss, they yearn for change. They are tired of famine, tired of poverty, tired of living in a never ending well of fear. They will restore Gondor's past glory; the crownless again shall be king.

summary: He cast himself into the long, burning fires of the chasm in order to perish. It was his intention to rid the world of the Silmaril he carried in his hand, burning his body, soul, will, and the bane of his existence. Thus, the Oath would have been fulfilled and he could have withdrawn into the deep shadows of the Halls of Mandos.But Fate had long before decided what his end was to be, and certainly not this one, for it was given to him to see the world once more. The Valar would have had no mercy on him to grant him another chance at life to set things right, he knew that. Instead, he had been drawn out of the depths of the flames by the thought of a stranger who seemed to belong neither among Elves, nor Men, nor Dwarves, an existence at first sight intriguing, but then dull, becoming one with her surroundings.The Silmaril was once again lost, once again far from the hands that bore the blood of Fëanor. And yet, at the same time, it was so close.As for him, he became the sole reason for her curiosity. Something she had never encountered before, someone who carried a curse perhaps greater and stronger than her own, which should have been impossible, for she was written outside of Time.

summary: “Creation was marred by Morgoth, in the days of Arda’s beginning. So much of our beautiful world was lost to his wars. My wish is to create a new world, one that will stand the test of time, a song whose melody shall only grow sweeter as the years trickle on. I believe that we few shall be the key to such a world, by erasing the foul reminders of a fouler past.”Imagine all the Maiar in Middle-earth reverting to their original mental state (you’ll be surprised how much story this changes), from the Spring of the World, before the passage of time began. Sauron and Saruman aren’t evil. The Blue Wizards are actually relevant. Radagast is… basically the same, just with a younger mind. The only Maia still as their present self is Gandalf, and only he and the Fellowship remember what it was like before this inexplicable change. The rest of Middle-earth is oblivious. Objects of significance like the Rings of Power still exist, just nobody realises their importance. I had a crazy brainwave here, and it may not make a lot of sense for most of it, but hey ho, we die like Finwë. It’s a double POV fic from both Gandalf and Frodo’s perspectives, by the way, and it alternates between chapters.Enjoy!

They’d defeated the darkness, they’d run the evil from Middle Earth, and there was so very little left to do before he and all the company found rest.The heartbreak they’d found in the Shire had been so very small compared to the trauma of the whole quest. And it had all turned out alright in the end, after all.Was he really supposed to be changing the peace at the end of his story?

“What’s strange?” he asks after a few seconds have passed.
Frodo skims his fingers just below the surface of the water.  “Being back here, I suppose,” he says, still in a soft, low tone. “I never thought….well, the last time we were here, it was beautiful, of course. But there was this dreadful business always looming over me. It never left my mind, not once. So I never got the chance to settle in and truly enjoy this place, not in the way Bilbo does. I had hoped, before, that if I did get the opportunity to come back things would be different. But it's…” he trails off. His hand hangs limply in the water. “It’s strange.”
 
The hobbits visit Rivendell once again on their homeward bound. Frodo tries to cope. Sam watches.

summary: Esther’s life is straightforward - long shifts at the flower shop, good coffee, and an impressive ability to avoid unnecessary drama. Sure, strange dreams and unexplainable memories creep in now and then, but she blames that on too much caffeine and not enough sleep.Then Ian and Leander show up: too tall, too graceful, and suspiciously out of place for two guys working at the local garden center. Ian has perfected brooding into an art form, and Leander seems to think life is one never-ending inside joke. Esther’s not sure what their deal is, but something about them feels… right. Or maybe just totally mad.As reality starts to fray at the edges, Esther begins to wonder if the universe is messing with her, or if something long lost is finally finding its way back to her.This story blends timelines (sometimes gracefully, sometimes not), familiar characters, plenty of brooding, and hopefully just the right amount of coffee.Expect slow burn, unresolved tension, and a flower shop that may or may not have deeper significance. summary:
“I forgive you,” Boromir says, just as grave as the captain before him, accepting his demotion to knighthood with far more grace than most would afford a too-bold babe. “An’ I dub you Sir ‘Rongil, so you must help protect nana. ‘Cos you’ve a real sword an’ can cut down real foes, until I have one, too, and can protect her better.”
 
 
 
So saying, he drives the point of the sword into the ground, and turns to face Finduilas, legs trembling a little with the effort to hold himself back from bouncing.
 
 
 
“No fear. No harm. Not while we’re here. So swear I.”
 
 
 
“So swear I,” Thorongil intones, after the fashion of the knights of old. Boromir turns back to him, taking both his hands to wrap them about the hilt of the toy sword, and for one selfish moment Finduilas is glad her son no longer faces her, that he might not see the tears spilling from her eyes.

Or her name rolling off his tongue and the sparkle in his eyes whenever he smiles at her. At the very least, it all might just end in a city of ruin.

summary: "Mairon remained alone in the temple, kneeling before the altar with his head bowed to the blood-slicked stone floor, with the air still hung heavy with the stench of iron and smoke. He stayed there until morning, motionless and silent, as if he, too, had turned to stone, being no different from the cold walls surrounding him. When the other priests or temple servants dared to enter, they always found him in the same place, his tall form remained unnervingly still, golden hair cascading over his shoulders in stark contrast to his black robes.Rumors spread quickly through the city, and all were amazen when, the very next day, Mairon appeared at the king’s councils. Or when he remained in the temple, not to sleep or rest through the daylight hours, but to receive any visitor who came seeking his guidance. Surely, such tireless devotion to his god and his duties could only be taken as proof of his sincerity and his holiness.And in this, at least, he had never lied."

summary: Año 1998 T. E. Kunnawyn nace en una fatídica noche de tormenta en la que su madre muere y su padre, un criador de caballos, se ve incapaz de cuidar de ella.
