Nadie sabe exactamente cómo acabó la niña en manos de los Enanos de las Montañas Grises, pero cuando cayó en manos de Dukona, señora enana de la colonia de Kibilul, Kunnawyn recibió un hombre enano y fue nombrada sucesora legítima. Así, en los inciertos tiempos que vivieron los Enanos de la Tercera Edad, corrió la voz sobre el peculiar origen de la heredera de Dukona y el futuro de Kibilul se tornó incierto. Los Orcos de Moria sometieron a Kibilul a asedio durante años. Kunnawyn, cansada de la burla y el odio de los orcos, se decide a cambiar el rumbo de los acontecimientos, sin saber que se convertirá en un personaje clave para la resistencia al avance del poder del Señor Oscuro en toda la región.

summary: "So." His voice was winter wind through dead branches. "The last of the great serpents of the North, brought low at last."She pressed her face against the bars of her cage, lips curling back from teeth that were too sharp for her human form."Pretty... king," she rasped, the words fighting their way past her unused throat. "Pretty... liar."Something flickered in those arctic eyes. "You still speak, then. My scouts said you were little more than a beast.""Beast..." She tasted the word, let it roll on her tongue like blood. Then she smiled, and saw several guards step back at the sight. "Beast... with... memory."She slammed against the bars, letting scales ripple across her skin for just a moment. "Remember... pretty king. Remember... fire. Remember... scream."Thranduil's hand twitched toward his face before he caught himself. He rose from his throne in one fluid motion and descended the steps, each movement precise as a dancer's. When he reached her cage, he stood just out of reach, studying her."I need your help," he said quietly.

summary: Did you watch Rings of Power 2x08 and wonder what was going through Galadriel’s head when she led a ragged band of refugees through a dark, forgotten tunnel to escape the flames and swords of besieged Eregion? When she traded herself to spare their lives? When she marched back to her former captor armed only with millennia of experience, her wits, and the Nine rings for mortal men? When she believed Elrond dead at his hand? Sauron's reappearance? Fighting the corrupted Maiar with all her strength? Shutting the door in her mind to him?When it wasn’t enough? When she fell?Me, too. The scenes probably amounted to 15 total minutes of screen time. This will be over 15,000 words fleshing them out. Written in past-tense, third-person limited. All spoken dialogue is directly from canon. This is a character study of Galadriel of the Noldor, daughter of the house of Finarfin, Commander of the Northern Armies of High King Gil-Galad — featuring: deep introspection; emotional turmoil; physical violence; the strength of the bonds of fellowship; promises broken and kept; duty; devotion; and feminine rage.

summary: It’s early spring in the village, the kind of warmth that seeps into your skin, just enough to make the air smell like blooming flowers, wet earth, and the faint tang of fresh grass. The town sits like a peaceful pocket tucked into the embrace of rolling hills, with winding cobbled streets and little shops that line the main road. You can hear the soft hum of daily life—chatter spilling from the baker’s window, the rustle of fabric from the tailor’s, and the clink of coins exchanged at the market square. It feels like a piece of history, preserved and gently breathing through time.It’s the first morning of your new life, and it’s already everything you imagined and nothing like you expected.A man—tall, broad-shouldered, and impossibly handsome in a way that you hadn’t quite prepared yourself for—stands beside the tractor. His hat is pulled low, his boots worn with age and use, and the most delightful little twinkle of mischief in his eye, as if he's been keeping this little joke to himself the entire ride. He doesn’t even look at you when you step down, but he does give the tractor’s worn wheel a final nudge, pulling it to a stop with an ease that screams ‘this is what I do, darlin’...

summary: **To New Beginnings**Friendship is an unbreakable bond that lasts forever. At least, that’s what Thranduil thought—until his best friend disappeared from the palace in the middle of the night without any explanation. Back then, he was the prince of Mirkwood. Now, he is the king.When Naira knocks on the palace gates once more, everything has changed. She doesn’t seem to recognize Thranduil, recoils from him, hides, and, in general, no longer appears to be the elf he once knew so well. The stories she has heard about him over the years have only instilled fear in her heart, leaving her terrified whenever she stands before the king. Thranduil, on the other hand, has spent all these years longing for nothing more than to have her back.Now that she is finally in front of him again, he swears to himself that he will never let her go. No matter the cost! He is determined to restore their friendship and find out if she has missed him as much as he has missed her. That his feelings for Naira go far beyond mere friendship is something he chooses to ignore—only making everything even worse.

summary: Elli was a typical woman and truly that was saying a lot. She had a typical life had being the key word. She died rather suddenly, but also rather predictably. Her death caused by none other then her current husband. Her life was one of hardship. She had been brilliant in high school. She was beautiful and strong, but all her family has seen was a chance to marry into a rich family. So they forced her at the age of 16 to marry a man she had never known before. Threats of  her never seeing her sibling spurred her into agreeing. Of course it all ended in disaster. She had one escape though and that was reading. The lord of the rings was her favorite.After it all happened Elli remembered that she never really believed much in a specific god, but if there was one she wanted them to be like the Valinor. She was shocked to find herself awake and alive in front of beings she could only describe as gods. She had been given a new body, a new name, and a task to help those she cared so much for. Only she wasn't sure what they meant or even who they referred to. Worst of all when she woke up she was rather confused and could remember very little beyond her new name and of course a vague idea of a mission.

summary: The sun hung lazily in the sky, spilling its golden warmth over the cliffs of Lindon, where the sea crashed in rhythmic applause against the shore. The scent of salt and wildflowers danced on the breeze, weaving through the tall grass that swayed at the cliff’s edge.Galadriel rolled her shoulders, stretching out the tension from the morning’s sparring. Sweat still lingered on her skin, the exhilarating rush of battle practice settling into a hum beneath her ribs. Her tunic clung to her back, her braids in disarray—hardly the picture of elegance, but she had never cared for that.What she had noticed, however, was the distinct lack of acknowledgment from her kin. No subtle smiles, no passing comments, no knowing glances. They had all seemed utterly preoccupied, as if this day—this very significant day—held no weight at all.She had not expected fanfare. Not really. But to be entirely forgotten? That was a sting she had not anticipated...

A tale of two idiots falling in love, and it only took them about three ages to figure it out…
Márafëa, an odd but talented Maiar, and Glorfindel, the famed Elven Hero, have been drawn to each other through the ages, remaining ever apart. From a fated meeting in Lórien's Garden to Márafëa tending Glorfindel's spirit in the Halls of Mandos after the Fall of Gondolin. It isn't until Márafëa is sent from Valinor as the sixth Istari that their adventure truly begins. Follow the duo as Márafëa learns what it means to be human, as they learn to fight together and tackle the Battle of Fornost, travel through Middle-earth, and help turn the tide in the War of the Ring.
Márafëa is tied to Sauron, to whom he once was, Mairon, her once-beloved brother. Someone Márafëa was fiercely protective of, then lost to the darkness of Melkor. Yet the connection remained, her love for him enduring. The Valar hope she will use that to her advantage; Márafëa fears it will pull her into Sauron's clutches. Luckily, Glorfindel will not let the shadows take his dear friend. He vows to keep Márafëa safe, to be her sunlight in the darkest of times, and hopes to one day be something more to her.

Jien stood by the window, fingers curled around a steaming cup of tea, letting its warmth seep into her skin. The scent of herbs, earthy and familiar, mixed with the crisp chill that bled through the wooden frame.This was home. Quiet. Steady. A life she had built with her own hands, far removed from the clash of swords and the thunder of war drums. She had chosen this—this solitude, this peace—though her small farm and its ever-growing collection of animals made sure she was never truly alone. It was a good life, if a simple one.The sudden knock at the door jolted her from her thoughts, her fingers tightening instinctively around the cup. A visitor? In this weather?..

The faint smell of aged parchment and ink hung in the air, a scent that wrapped around you like a warm cloak. summary: Galion has always felt like he didn’t fit in his own skin. After deciding to live truly and freely as the type of elf he wanted to be, he was abandoned and discarded by his birth family. There are still many that criticize him for his non-traditional lifestyle, but he slowly learns to respect and stand up for himself. The one thing he never expects to find, however, is true love. Will he be another brief flirtation? Just a temporary distraction in a moment of time? Or can love sprout in the most barren of soil? What if that love is lost? They are cursed to carry their torment like a second heartbeat, their fractured family haunted by the memory of what was stolen—and the horrors yet to come.The youngest sister, with trembling resolve and bloodied hands, made the ultimate sacrifice to tether her siblings together, forging a bond even the void cannot sever. But unity comes at a cost, and Durnhart Manor stands as a testament to their unraveling. Every step they take through its decayed corridors draws them closer to the abyss, and the question lingers: will they find strength in their cursed bond, or will the very darkness they wield consume them whole?

summary: It is meant to be a quiet departure, but nothing ever is for those who have burned their bridges and left the ashes behind.Uchiha Itachi dies. She knows this. She remembers the blood, the pain, the weight of her sins. That is meant to be the end of her story. But it isn’t.Instead, Itachi wakes in another world—a world of ageless faces, whispered songs of starlight, and shadows older than anything she’s known. A world of elves, men, and ancient evil, where her sins follow her in the form of shadows that twist and writhe beneath her skin. Here, in a place where light shines brighter and darkness sinks deeper, she is not forgiven, only cursed to endure.She tells herself it doesn’t matter. It never has. Itachi has always endured—loneliness, agony, death, and now eternity. She slips through the halls of Rivendell like a wraith, unseen, unheard, her silent existence a defiance of the life she no longer wants. title: The Linguistic Situation of Third-Age Middle Earth
author: wonn
fandoms: The Lord of the Rings - J. R. R. Tolkien
summary: The Red Book of Westmarch makes it clear that Middle-Earth was a very linguistically diverse location; however, much of that diversity is not shown in the narrative itself, which portrays characters as speaking 'Westron' or 'the Common Speech' among each other. This seems difficult to believe given Middle-Earth as the book describes it, and is much more likely a device for narrative convenience rather than an accurate portrayal of the situation. This paper attempts to look beyond the conceit of Westron to discern what the linguistic situation in late Third Age Middle-Earth likely actually was, and what that can tell us about what might have actually happened when characters in the Red Book interacted with each other.

Líreth looked at him, her breath hitching in her chest, as if the question had pierced straight through her defenses. She had spent so long running from attachments, from emotions, from the very idea of needing someone. But in this moment, with him, she could not deny it any longer.

kindlingkɪndlɪŋuncountable nounKindling is small pieces of dry wood and other materials that you use to start a fire.***Aragorn had not thought of her in years. Not when the shadow of war darkened the horizon, nor when the whispers of Sauron’s return stirred the hearts of men with dread, nor even when the One Ring was revealed, bearing the weight of all their fates. No, such memories had been left behind, buried beneath the long toil of exile and the burden of his calling. There was no room for heartache amidst the tide of destiny.
Yet when he saw her again upon the steps of Meduseld, the world seemed to still. Her dark hair fell like raven’s wings, and her eyes—deep and blue as the waters of Tarn Aeluin. She stood tall, proud and unyielding, yet there was in her bearing the same grace he remembered, the same quiet strength that had once stirred his heart.
In that moment, all he had fought to forget surfaced, unbidden, like leaves rising from the depths of a still pool. He felt the pull of her presence, a tether that no distance or passing age could sever. He longed to be near her, to speak the words he had long left unsaid, to hold her as though the world itself could be set aside.

Als Sohn der Besitzer des Microsensor-Unternehmens HOBBIT wird Bilbo auf eine gefährliche und unerwartete Mission geschickt, um sich gegen ORKs dunkle Machenschaften zu stellen. An seiner Seite stehen dreizehn ungewöhnliche Verbündete, darunter der charismatische Geschäftserbe Thorin und noch dazu der rätselhafte Gandalf. Gemeinsam kämpfen sie gegen ein Unternehmen, das alles zerstören will, was ihnen lieb ist. Es erwarten sie brenzlige Abenteuer, unerwartete Freundschaften und die Enthüllung skrupelloser Skandale, die Bilbo an seine Grenzen bringen. In dieser modernen Version von Mittelerde gibt es keine Magie, sondern eine Welt voller Intrigen, Machtspiele und Korruption. Wird Bilbo den Mut finden, sich gegen Arzok zu stellen und diese oligarche  Welt verändern? Begleite ihn auf ein Abenteuer, das Tolkiens Klassiker mit einer spannenden, zeitgenössischen Geschichte verbindet.

tags: Other Additional Tags to Be Added
summary: Fëanor stood at the edge of the glittering lake, some strange feeling building in his chest. He had been so certain of their path, of what measures he and his people would need to make in this strange new world. But even as he went to set fire to the ships that had taken them over the waters, away from those he had somehow thought as traitors, a great storm had arose and the wind had stung them on the beach with such a force that it had put out the torches one by one...before they ever had a chance to touch the ships and set them alight.It felt like that same wind had driven something from him. Some strange madness that had been building for days. His head ached and his limbs felt heavy and strange. The storm had driven them back from the waters and by the time the skies had cleared once more it felt as though he could think again. He had sent the ships back over the water and had taken his people inwards, not waiting for the others, knowing that they would need to find some clean water and a good camp to take stock and gather their strength for what was to come.

summary:
It is… a memory? Yes, a memory. He was young and going to war. He was perhaps afraid, perhaps keen, perhaps both; he had not yet lost all that he is still to lose. And this… this night happened, he is sure – he remembers – he relives it, campfire smoke in the cold air, the bright stars above. Singing, around him -

  Some small and desperate part of him tears at his mind – these are orcs you hear, these are orcs, you know the tune, that’s all, they’ve stolen it and distorted it and sullied it like they do all else, it’s not your songs, it’s not your comrades -

  - but his lips mouth the words of the song all the same.

Zumindest dachte Thranduil das, bis seine beste Freundin mitten in der Nacht ohne Grund aus dem Schloss verschwand. Damals war er der Prinz des Düsterwaldes, mittlerweile ist er der König.Als Naira wieder an die Tore des Schlosses klopft, hat sich alles verändert. Sie scheint Thranduil nicht wiederzuerkennen, zuckt vor ihm zurück, versteckt sich und scheint allgemein nicht mehr die Elbin zu sein, die Thranduil einmal so gut kannte. All die Geschichten, die sie während der vergangenen Jahre über ihn gehört hat, haben dafür gesorgt, dass sie jetzt nur noch panische Angst empfindet, wenn sie dem König gegenübersteht. Thranduil hingegen hat sich all die Jahre nichts sehnlicher gewünscht, als sie wieder bei sich zu haben.Als sie ihm endlich wieder gegenüber steht, schwört er sich, sie nicht mehr gehenzulassen. Egal was es kostet! Er will die Freundschaft mit Naira wieder erneuern und herausfinden, ob sie sich genauso nach ihm gesehnt hat, wie er sich nach ihr. Dass seine Gefühle für die Elbin weit über Freundschaft hinausgehen, ignoriert er und verschlimmert damit alles nur noch mehr.

summary:
"You see," Elrond smugly informed him, "as I rose this morning, I had a strange and very intelligent question in my mind. In this land of many elves, who is the oldest in age?"
  "I suppose it must be easy to guess," Aragorn said slowly. "Surely-"
  "Yes, my foster-son," Elrond patted Aragorn on the back. It was a gesture that was so unlike any gesture of love in these recent years that Aragorn froze, locking eyes with Glorfindel who gave him a cheery grin and enthusiastic thumbs-up. "I am glad that your self-awareness has increased since your days of youth. It is you, after all, that is the oldest among us all."

summary: After the War of Wrath, Mairon comes to see Eönwë.He was still beautiful, though pitiful to behold: matted hair framing a colourless face, shabby rags clinging to a body just as pallid under layers of dirt. His eyes were the only part of him that seemed alive. They looked strikingly innocent for one known for ruthless cruelty.Vanity and pride had always been his flaws, even before his fall. To appear before the herald of Manwë in such an unkept state was a sign of how much he had changed. Or was it a trick to fool him? To pluck at the strings of his heart so as to awaken his sympathy? Elrond followed, curls sticking to his brow as he surveyed the room through narrowed, dark eyes. Inside, the murmur of conversation dulled as they entered. Human men—drunk, slouched, and smelling of stale ale—shifted uncomfortably but kept their eyes on the strangers.Galadriel swept a glance over the room, unimpressed, and strode toward the counter. Ця пісня — ніби власноруч створена музика, а Аннатар, як і усі майяр, чутливий до неї — пісня творіння все ще бринить десь глибоко у його свідомості. Келебрімбор — вибагливий і норовистий інструмент, він нагадує поперечну флейту, в якій немає прямого видобування звуку. Не можна прикласти до неї губи, дмухнути і отримати його на виході, як із простіших сородичів. Повітря треба вміло скеровувати, та, навіть за найсприятливіших обставин, “звучатимуть” лише тридцять відсотків від докладених зусиль. Так і ельф — сприймає далеко не всі його посили, і тому доводиться докладати все більше і більше зусиль.Пісня будить Саурона — ту частину особистості, яку Аннатар старанно ховає від усіх оточуючих, щоб не налякати їх раніше, ніж потрібно. Саурон зацікавлено дослухається. На його думку у сплетінні звуків не вистачає болю — нотка відчаю зробила б мелодію пікантнішою. Аннатар погоджується, але впевнено гасить будь-який жорстокий намір. Не час. Він ще не вичерпав свої можливості. Те, чого прагне Саурон — зброя останньої надії.

summary: The afternoon sun draped Rivendell in a warm golden glow, casting sparkles over the leaves that had begun to turn vibrant shades of amber and gold. It was the kind of day that practically begged for fresh air and fun, especially for one particular two-year-old with an endless supply of energy.Liel, the spirited nephew of Galadriel and Elrond, was a bundle of joy and mischief, and his brown curls bounced wildly with every tiny step he took. He was racing through the lush grass, his giggles ringing out like a cheerful melody that echoed through the valley. With his wide, curious eyes sparkling with mischief, he darted around like a little deer, expertly evading Elrond’s outstretched arms. For someone so small, Liel had mastered the art of escape: each time Elrond thought he had him, Liel would squeal with delight and take off in the opposite direction, the soft autumnal green of his tunic already smeared with the evidence of his little adventures. Dirt smudged his knees, and there were faint traces of whatever he had been snacking on earlier, possibly a few crumbs from those famous elven lembas biscuits one may say.

title: The Wake
author: quintessence_of_dust
fandoms: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power (TV 2022)
summary:
Another round of boisterous song started up at the table nearest him, and Elrond took a long drink from his cup to avoid the frown he could feel pulling at his mouth. This was the custom under the mountain, he knew: to celebrate a life well lived, rather than mourn its end, and he did not begrudge the dwarves their traditions. Still, it was not the way he would grieve, if he had his choice. His heart ached and he wanted quiet: a moment to himself, with fresh air in his lungs and familiar voices in his ears, a sky above his head rather than stone. He wanted company that did not grate on his frayed nerves and someone who understood why he did not wish to celebrate; he wanted his friend back.

  
    Or: many years after the events of The Rings of Power, King Durin IV has died of old age. Tomorrow, his daughter Gerda will become king of Khazad-Dûm. Tonight, Elrond attends his friend's wake.

summary:
Es begab sich im März des Jahres 2989 des Dritten Zeitalters, 1389 nach Auenland-Zeitrechnung, dass Bilbo Beutlin, mit einigen Freunden trinken ging und später an diesem Abend nicht nach Hause zurückkehrte.Selbstverständlich wurden Ermittlungen von mehr und weniger großer Ernsthaftigkeit durchgeführt, von Leuten, die mal mehr, mal weniger Befugnis dazu hatten. Da jedoch niemand tatsächlich zugegen gewesen war, um einen Unfall oder ein Verschwinden zu sehen, konnte der Fall niemals aufgeklärt werden, und die Auenland-Hobbits mussten sich mit der Tatsache begnügen, dass das Zweite Verschwinden von Bilbo Beutlin, wie der Vorfall im Volksmund irgendwann genannt wurde, ein ungelöstes Rätsel bleiben würde.
Eines Tages, lange bevor die Ereignisse des "Herrn der Ringe" sich zutragen, verschwindet Bilbo Beutlin (wieder mal) spur- und grußlos aus dem Auenland. Dieses Mal sichert sich jedoch Lobelia Sackheim-Beutlin Beutelsend - und auch den rätselhaften Zauberring, den Bilbo zurückgelassen hat. Von da an verlaufen die Dinge ziemlich anders.

summary: “We have a latecomer,” Elrond announced lightly enough. “The heir to Steward Denethor of Gondor.”Boromir's lifeless eyes looked a thousand miles away. His armor, engraved with the White Tree, was scuffed and battered, his royal cloak torn and burned at the edges. A deep, jagged slash ran over the bridge of his nose, glistening with blood.The Council, which had gained a base level of volume from quiet discussions, fell into a sharp silence. The heir to the Steward of Gondor pulled himself to his feet, the simple action looking like it took all his remaining willpower.“What news of Gondor?” Elrond prompted, though his eyes carried unfathomable age.There was a heavy pause. “Gondor—” His voice was hoarse and cracked harshly, as though even speaking the words was a painful act. “Gondor has fallen.”——Mordor makes a risky gamble in their military advancements and it pays off. Gondor falls, and all hope in Arda falls with it. With the greatest defenses now lost, the time now goes to the lesser legends, the most Golden Alliances, and a Fellowship that is much the same.Here is a world that is infinitely darker that the original, but hope lives nonetheless.

They met each other’s gaze. Neither would fully yield; each held their ground in a dance of equals. Control passed between them like a tangible force, ebbing and flowing. Anárien’s hips moved with confidence, matching Elrond’s powerful thrusts. It was a cosmic interplay, like two supernovae orbiting one another, each refusing to be pulled entirely into the other’s gravity until they finally collided, clashed, exploded.
  
  
    “Now,” she commanded, her voice thick with desire.
  
  
    Elrond’s control shattered.
  
They've danced around each other for centuries—Elrond with his careful restraint, Anárien with her fearless independence. But behind their friendship lies something far more potent, something neither can ignore any longer. How fierce can the flames burn when centuries of desire finally ignite?

But it’s face-side might yet seek the words of his beloved to draw the whole away from the railing.”
  “Aye, aye,” Gimli nodded, frowning at the long swathe of Legolas’ hair, fluttering about in the breeze beyond the glass confines around them.
Legolas is a selkie who cannot find his pelt, but Gimli does not know that. All he knows is that his lover came upon the lighthouse he and Aragorn tended one night, wandering and confused and asking for a warm place to dry off. He stayed with them for many long months, and now has claimed Gimli's heart, though his own has seemed to grow restless, his eyes ever-turned to the sea.Gimli is desperate to know what ails his lover, but it seems that it would take more than pleas and urges to get it out of him.A day at the market does the trick.

summary:
Aragorn had truly thought Boromir was dead.
 They all did, but especially Aragorn — he was the one who broke the arrows, he was the one who laid his mouth upon his fallen brother-in-arms, his friend, and tried to become as Boromir’s breath, again and again, continually breathing for him, checking for a pulse that wouldn’t come.Gimli had to pull him off of Boromir’s cooling body. Strong, thick dwarvish hands shaking even as he so firmly pulled Aragorn into a firm hug, red beard wet and shining with his weeping even as he held Aragorn close to him and consoled him, telling him, You’ve done all you can for him, laddie — all you can. By Mahal, I know this is true, lad. You’ve done all you can, and none can do naught for him more. Gently, into Aragorn’s heaving chest, No, not even you, Aragorn.  …a mournful and bitterly sweet laugh barks out of Aragorn’s aching throat as he sits beneath the white tree and weeps, “and yet he lives,” Aragorn whispers to himself, to all of Gondor, to no one in particular. He laughs again,  cries even harder, 
  “And yet he lives.”

  June 12th, 2024 - summary updated

summary:
Thranduil returns from Dol Guldur introducing Legolas as his son, though the truth is far more complicated. Slowly Thranduil finds himself consumed with Legolas, and becomes entangled in a desperate struggle between light and darkness.---Thranduil has many questions. Why? What had Lanthir done to deserve such a fate, at the hands of her child, no less? Had Legolas been possessed, or was it pure evil that ran through his veins and encouraged him to bring forth his mother’s fate? But he could not bring himself to ask. He made an attempt to convince himself that it was because Legolas had made a mistake, a terrible mistake that he would regret for the rest of his unending life. In the child’s face, Thranduil finds no falsehood. No ill will, aside from the urge to survive at any cost. Perhaps it had been a terrible misunderstanding, resulting in the worst possible outcome.
  But, Thranduil thinks to himself grimly, he knows the true reason he does not ask. He does not ask because he cannot bear to hear the answer, the confirmation of the damning blood that runs through this child’s veins. Cannot bear to lose this last small piece of Lanthir along with all he has lost today.

tags: the Line of Luthien means certain things
summary:
Elrond has just awoken to find himself a prisoner in an Enemy camp. He has a concussion, and he is surrounded by three very young (and scared) elves. None of whom he recognizes, and all of whom are looking to him for leadership in making an escape attempt. In the planning of which, it doesn’t take Elrond long to figure out that he lost something, when he was hit on the head. Specifically, about an Age’s worth of memories.
“It will be easier to escape from this camp now,” said Elrond, “before they take us all the way back to Angband.”
It was Thranduil, who, with a light of horrible comprehension dawning in his eyes, then asked, "Elrond, when do you think it is? I mean, what year?"
“I'd rather lost track of the days, even before that blow to the head,” Elrond admitted carefully, “So I'm not sure whether it's still Year 572 of the First Age of the Sun, or if it is already Year 573.”
“Um. No, it’s not,” Thranduil corrected, with a wince.
It really wasn't.

The Elves had all but turned their backs on her, but he rode through water, fire, and dangerous land by her side—all the while knowing she sought him out in order to end his existence, but he pretended he was something else. He had used her need for retaliation against her to serve his own means, to entrap his own enemy, and he did it all with a smile on his face.The hand upon her hilt shook ever so slightly, and a familiar voice called out to her from the shadows.“Losing your resolve already?” he teased her in light mockery, a hint of laughter echoing afterwards. It resonated in the den of darkness before her, a haunting song that seemed to fill her ears to the brim with each echo. Predator and prey, but who was the hunter and who was the prey?

summary: Though he was the Valar to preside over the dead, Namo found joy in watching life. There was one race in particular that he found he could interact with without having them cower in subservience or fear. The hobbits were full of life. During their years of wandering, Namo found himself taking them under his care. He helped them find the Shire and build a life there. Not every hobbit could hear his deep voice when he whispered to them. Even fewer could see his shadowed form when he walked amongst them. Only a brush with death brought certain hobbits closer to him. When the Fell Winter struck, he called many of his children home to him.There was one, however, that Namo pronounced his Doom with a heavy heart. One who would have to suffer living in a cruel world for many years before he could find peace. One who Namo cradled in his hands during that terrible winter and then released back into the world of the living a changed hobbit. One who could not only hear and see Namo but had become so intertwined with his power that he could deliver Dooms to others if their fate was strong enough.

summary: Erestor knelt, hand pressed to the cold earth. The woods about him were still and silent, not even a whisper of wind stirring the bows. Thick, black clouds had lined the horizon in the north when Erestor had entered the forest, a foreboding sight. Erestor pressed his lips together, torn. He had to go north. It was all he could think of. He had to go north. He had to reach Angband. What he would do after that he was not sure, but surely, surely there was a reason why he was sent back, why Elrond sent him back, when the first waves of Sauron's armies had crested the pass that led to Imladris.

summary: "No," he said gently, taking a deep breath. "No, I will not be returning home this time. I have been - Well, I myself swore it - asked to go on a quest, at the behest of Lord Elrond, on the behalf of all Elves. 'Tis secret, so I may not say much, but all races of the Free People are represented - Estel goes! and Boromir as well - and there are nine of us. But the quest will take me far from home and it is perilous, very perilous. A fool's hope, I believe Tauriel called it" - his second gave a terse nod and would not meet his eyes - "but if it succeeds - if it succeeds, the Shadow is banished forever. Our home will be safe from all enemies and truly will be Greenwood again. All homes and havens will be safe, for the Enemy will be no more. Isildur's Bane has been discovered, and it is the choice of the Wise that it must be destroyed if the Shadow is ever to fall. I am one of this company, though Lord Elrond refrains from confirming this in as many words whilst he deliberates, and I am sworn to go some of the way with him. I, as you, remember the dishonour that lost her the position the last time she held it, yet I would suggest that honour has no place in a war such as the one that comes now, and that skill should be the only thing to endure.
